headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Paolo Banchero suffered a low-grade high ankle sprain and could miss 4-to-6 weeks.
body: Banchero tweaked his right ankle early in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves. The 23-year-old forward returned after going to the locker room, but the team shut him down midway through the fourth quarter. A high ankle sprain could sideline Banchero for 4-to-6 weeks, which is potentially devastating news for the 0-2 Magic. Orlando will the face the Knicks on Sunday and at this point it’s unlikely Banchero suits up with Tristan da Silva being the most likely to replace him in the starting lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Yaxel Lendeborg notched 18 points (4-of-11 FGs, 9-of-12 FTs), 13 rebounds, six assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
body: After a much-discussed debut in the Warriors’ loss to the Lakers on Wednesday, Lendeborg recorded his first career double-double on Friday. The rookie’s final stat line lacked only a blocked shot, but he has all the makings of a player who will offer consistent value in fantasy basketball. Stephen Curry (ankle) is not expected to play in Saturday’s game against the Suns, and Brandin Podziemski (back) has already been ruled out. If Lendeborg is sitting on your league’s waiver wire, don’t hesitate to pick him up.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandin Podziemski (head) accounted for 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, three steals, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
body: Podziemski entered Friday’s game dealing with a sore lower back that kept him out of Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers. It didn’t help matters that he took an inadvertent forearm from Grizzlies center Zach Edey to the head early in the first quarter. Podziemski returned later in the period after a trip to the locker room and logged 33 minutes overall. He finished with a complete stat line, but this is it for Podz in Week 1. After Friday’s defeat, he said he would not play in Saturday’s game against the Suns.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Graham Ike produced 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
body: After starting Draymond Green at center in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr opted against that approach on Friday. As a result, Ike made his first NBA start. The rookie from Gonzaga shot reasonably well, but he offered little value beyond points and three-pointers. The Warriors visit Phoenix on Saturday, and Ike may play more, as Al Horford hasn’t played both games of back-to-backs in a few years.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephen Curry tallied 24 points (5-of-15 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
body: Curry led the Warriors in scoring on Friday, but he shot a frigid 5-of-15 from the field. The assists were solid, but this was not the best night to have the Warriors star in most fantasy lineups. After the game, Curry said he “probably” won’t play against the Suns on Saturday, bad news for fantasy managers hoping for a bounce-back effort.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: GG Jackson finished Friday’s win over the Warriors with two points (1-of-6 FGs), four rebounds and one assist.
body: With Cedric Coward (wrist) unavailable, Jackson moved into the starting lineup on Friday. Unfortunately for those who streamed him, GG offered little value as a spot starter. He picked up four fouls in 10 first-half minutes, and Kris Murray (three rebounds, one assist, and one block) would start the third quarter. Whether or not Jackson gets another opportunity on Sunday against the Kings depends on Coward’s health, but he may not be worth the streaming risk in most leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Stewart notched four points (2-of-3 FGs), two rebounds and one steal in Friday’s win over the Warriors.
body: Stewart made his official Grizzlies debut on Friday, playing most of his minutes when starting center Zach Edey (8/10/3/1/2) was not on the floor. Unfortunately, Beef Stew picked up four fouls in the first half, including three in the first quarter, which limited him to 16 minutes. It remains to be seen what his role will look like once the ankle is no longer a concern, but Stewart isn’t someone worth rostering in most redraft leagues just yet.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylen Wells recorded 17 points (5-of-9 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Warriors.
body: After recording 12 points and four steals in Wednesday’s season-opening win over the Jazz, Wells was more productive offensively against the Warriors. He scored an efficient 17 points, a number he met or exceeded in 18 of 69 appearances last season. Wells still isn’t at the point where he’s a must-roster player, but he should have more room to produce, especially on nights when Cedric Coward (wrist) doesn’t play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ty Jerome accounted for 28 points (11-of-22 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Warriors.
body: After scoring 45 points in Wednesday’s opener, Jerome appeared to be coming down to earth in the first half of Friday’s game. However, after scoring eight first-half points on 3-of-7 shooting, the Grizzlies point guard put up 14 points in the third quarter. Jerome and the Grizzlies ripped off a 17-0 run in the fourth to move to 2-0 on the season, getting their four-game road trip off to a good start.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Boozer finished Friday’s win over the Warriors with 25 points (6-of-13 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), 13 rebounds, six assists, two steals and four three-pointers.
body: After struggling with his shot in his NBA debut on Wednesday, Boozer had a much better night against the Warriors. The rookie forward made four of his first five three-point attempts and scored 14 points in the first half. By the end of the night, Boozer had made franchise history, becoming the second-youngest Grizzly to record a double-double. Memphis ends its Week 1 with a game against the Kings on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Garland finished Friday’s loss to the Lakers with 26 points (9-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six assists, one steal and four three-pointers.
body: The star guards in this matchup all seemed to struggle with turnovers. Garland racked up nine, while the Lakers’ Luka Dončić (11) and Austin Reaves (six) combined for 17. Garland had a solid night shooting the basketball, but nine-cat managers took a hit because of the turnovers. He’ll look to finish Week 1 on a high note when the Clippers visit the Thunder on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brook Lopez tallied 22 points (8-of-9 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, three blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: While Isaiah Jackson (six points, six rebounds, three assists, three steals, and one block in 28 minutes) earned the starting center role, his limited offensive skill set means Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue will continue to factor Lopez into his plans. Against the Lakers, the 7-foot-1 backup scored 15 points on 6-of-6 shooting in the first half on Friday. Lopez’s production tailed off after halftime, but his final line reminded everyone what he can do, even in a backup role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Donovan Clingan scored 8 points (3-of-5 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), ten rebounds, three assists, and two blocks in 19 minutes against the Kings.
body: Clingan had some foul trouble in this game and the Blazers went small which resulted in lower minutes for Clingan. He still produced when he was out there, but it was obviously not what you were hoping for. This happened last year at times and there will be more games this year where its in the best of the Blazers to have him on the bench. He’ll have his next opportunity against the Lakers where he will need to play more minutes against Walker Kessler.

headline: Rui Hachimura recorded 16 points (5-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Playing against his former team for the first time since signing with the Clippers in free agency, Hachimura struggled with his shot. He’s started slowly, shooting 8-of-27 from the field in the Clippers’ first two games. Given the team’s lack of reliable scorers, the shot volume will be there. However, it won’t mean much if Hachimura can’t hit shots at a higher clip. He’s a career 49.8 percent shooter, which suggests that Rui will turn things around. But things won’t get any easier, as the Clippers visit the Thunder on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Damian Lillard with 19 points (7-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, two steals, a block and two 3-pointers in Blazers win over the Kings.
body: It wasn’t the most efficient night for Damian Lillard, but he still gave you a good game. As he’s coming back from his Achilles injury, he will have some nights where he is not very efficient, especially early on the season. We weren’t drafting Damian Lillard as high as we have been, so there isn’t much to complain about when there’s the occasional inefficient night.

headline: Matisse Thybulle accounted for 13 points (5-of-8 FGs), one rebound, two assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Clippers.
body: Could Thybulle return to relevance in fantasy basketball with the Lakers? His defense earned the veteran wing a starting spot, and he played well on both ends of the floor in Friday’s win. In addition to his three defensive contributions, Thybulle shot 3-of-6 from beyond the arc. He’s a career 34.9 percent shooter from deep, so managers shouldn’t expect high-level production there. However, the starting role makes Thybulle someone to watch, especially in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyshawn George had 11 points (2-of-9 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals, and a three against Raptors.
body: He did get to the line seven times and got you two steals which provided some value because he didn’t hit many shots and gave you unwanted turnovers. The Raptors physicality clearly bothered George in this game as he had 8 turnovers in this game. Until AJ comes back, he’s still worth rostering in redraft leagues.

headline: Ty Jerome, Jaylen Wells, GG Jackson, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey will start Friday’s game against the Warriors.
body: The Grizzlies are without Cedric Coward, who suffered a sprained left wrist during Wednesday’s win over the Jazz. Jackson moves into the starting lineup, making him a worthwhile streamer in deep leagues. The other four starters are unchanged.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is available for Friday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Stewart has been cleared to make his Grizzlies debut after spraining his ankle during the preseason. He’ll provide frontcourt depth off the bench, likely resulting in fewer minutes for Quinten Post.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tre Johnson scored 20 points (7-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), and got two rebounds, a steal, and four 3-pointers against the Raptors.
body: Tre Johnson can absolutely score the ball, and he didn’t do much else in this game. While the fantasy upside is not very high for Tre Johnson, he’s useful as a streamer if you’re looking for points and three’s boost. In this current construction of the Wizards roster, he’s just a 6 th man type.

headline: Cedric Coward (wrist) is out for Friday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Initially doubtful with a sprained left wrist, Coward is officially out for Friday’s game. GG Jackson replaces him in the starting lineup and is worth streaming in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Davis with 9 points (3-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, a steal, two blocks on Friday.
body: After Anthony’s 30-point double-double, Davis had a down game against the Raptors. They really forced him into some turnovers, and he didn’t hit as many shots. The truth of who Anthony Davis is as a player is somewhere in the middle between his first game, and this game. Don’t panic and go onto the next one.

headline: Trae Young with 22 points (5-of-15 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), one rebound, twelve assists, one steal, and four 3-pointers against the Raptors in the 112-102 loss.
body: Another inefficient night from Trae Young, but he got you the numbers you wanted from him. They were going against the Raptors, so there was a lot of inefficiency across the board. He will have better shooting nights, so don’t panic. That being said, he’s not the most efficient guard in the NBA.

headline: Wendell Carter Jr. amassed 20 points (8-of-9 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), nine rebounds, one assist, two blocks and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
body: The offseason signing of Nikola Vučević hasn’t hurt Carter’s playing time, as Vooch has been third in Orlando’s center pecking order in the first two games. After logging 31 minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the Hawks, Carter played 29 minutes against the Timberwolves and led the Magic in points, rebounds, blocks, and three-pointers. He’s never been a great fantasy option, especially in category leagues, but Carter’s start to the season has been encouraging.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Desmond Bane accounted for five points (2-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, one steal and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
body: Bane had a night to forget, struggling on both ends of the floor before fouling out with 10:31 remaining in the fourth quarter. The Magic guard shot 1-of-9 from beyond the arc and offered little value beyond his lone steal. Given his track record, fantasy managers who are rostering Bane shouldn’t panic over one performance. He’ll look to bounce back on Sunday when the Magic visit the Knicks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Franz Wagner tallied 18 points (7-of-14 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
body: Wagner played 32 minutes before fouling out of Friday’s defeat with a little over three minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. While he shot a solid overall field-goal percentage, the Magic forward made 3-of-6 from the foul line and committed six turnovers. Over two games, Wagner has recorded 10 assists and nine turnovers, something he’ll need to clean up. Orlando ends its Week 1 with a game against the Knicks on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Steven Adams (calf) is available for Friday’s game against the Spurs.
body: A game-time call for Friday’s game, Adams is good to go for his first appearance of the season. His availability likely pushes Clint Capela out of the rotation entirely, with Capela having logged eight minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Paolo Banchero (ankle) has returned to Friday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Banchero tweaked his right ankle early in the third quarter, forcing him to head to the locker room. He has since returned to action, which is great for Magic fans and fantasy managers alike.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Paolo Banchero (ankle) returned to the Magic locker room during the third quarter of Friday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Banchero appeared to tweak his right ankle while crashing for a rebound early in the third quarter after colliding with teammate Jalen Suggs. He has since gone back to the locker room for further evaluation. Tristan da Silva has entered the lineup and should play more if Banchero can’t return.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luke Kennard (knee) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Kennard did not play in Wednesday’s season-opening loss to the Trail Blazers, and his absence led to Jordan Goodwin playing 22 minutes off the bench. Goodwin’s playing time may suffer if Kennard returns.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cooper Flagg (shoulder) heads to the locker room early holding his shoulder.
body: Cooper Flagg got hit from a hard foul and went to the locker room early to get his shoulder checked on.

headline: Oso Ighodaro (oblique) is doubtful for Saturday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Ighodaro, initially believed to have suffered a hip injury during Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers, has been diagnosed with an oblique strain. His absence on Saturday would likely result in Duop Reath playing rotation minutes off the bench, with Khaman Maluach remaining the starting center.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandin Podziemski (back) is available for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Podziemski is available after sitting out Wednesday’s season-opening loss to the Lakers. His return likely pushes De’Anthony Melton to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Reed Sheppard (knee) ruled out against Spurs
body: Reed bumped his knee in the opener against Dallas. Expect more Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic in his place. Reed wasn’t impacting most fantasy leagues anyway.

headline: Keldon Johnson (mouth) is available to play on Friday against the Rockets.
body: Keldon Johnson suffered a laceration in his mouth against the Thunder. He will be available and likely play as normal. He can be used as a streamer for points and rebounds.

headline: De’Aaron Fox (wrist) is available for Friday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Fox’s sprained right wrist will not keep him out of Friday’s game. He’ll take on his usual starting point guard duties as the Spurs look to rebound from Tuesday’s loss to the Thunder.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaime Jaquez Jr. had 19 points (7-of-11 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), 11 rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers against the Bulls on Friday.
body: Jaquez had another excellent game for the Bucks and appears to be one of the big winners in terms of increased fantasy value from the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade. The only drawback on Friday was that he turned the ball over six times after turning it over twice in his Bucks debut.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Spencer Jones (hamstring) is out for Saturday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: The Nuggets aren’t going to take any chances with Jones, who’s working his way back from a strained hamstring. Rookie Trevon Brazile played 18 minutes off the bench in his debut and grabbed 12 rebounds. He’s likely to take on a similar role as Aaron Gordon’s backup on Saturday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Alpha Diallo (wrist) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Diallo played 22 minutes in his Nuggets’ debut on Thursday, starting the second half for the injured Cameron Johnson (ankle). With Johnson ruled out for Saturday, Diallo could start Denver’s home opener if he’s available. If not, DeMar DeRozan may start.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tyler Herro had 34 points (12-of-24 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Bulls.
body: Not only did Herro lead the Bucks in shots for the second consecutive game, he took twice as many field goal attempts as any of his teammates against the Bulls. Despite the high usage, Herro only had one turnover, which is important for his value in nine-category leagues. If he can continue to control his turnover total, Herro could be in line for the best fantasy season of his career.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Cameron Johnson (ankle) is out for Saturday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Johnson sprained his right ankle during the second quarter of Thursday’s loss to the Thunder and did not return. Alpha Diallo started the third quarter, but he’s questionable for Saturday’s game. If Diallo can’t play, the Nuggets may turn to DeMar DeRozan from the start.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Leonard Miller had 19 points (7-of-11 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Friday.
body: Miller only played 23 minutes off the bench in this one as Caleb Wilson and Norman Powell were the only Bulls to play at least 30 minutes. Still, it’s impossible to ignore Miller’s production after an impressive preseason and the first two games of the regular season. He’s scored in double figures in both games despite minutes totals in the low-20s. Miller probably needs more minutes to be fantasy-relevant, but at some point he could force his way into a more prominent role in the rotation.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Caleb Wilson had 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Friday.
body: After Wilson’s inauspicious debut Wednesday that included 33.3 percent shooting from the field and nine turnovers, the 20-year-old forward bounced back nicely in the second game of his NBA career. He was 7-of-14 from the field (50 percent), scored 21 points and had just three turnovers. Wilson will have ups and downs in his career and there will certainly be more bumps in the road during his rookie season, but this was undoubtedly a promising performance.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Norman Powell had 25 points (7-of-20 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in the Bulls’ 132-125 victory over the Hawks on Friday.
body: Powell was the Bulls’ leading scorer in the victory over the Bucks on Wednesday. While he had 25 points, Powell’s typically excellent shooting from behind the three-point line was noticeably absent. The 33-year-old shooting guard went 2-of-12 from behind the arc and is now 4-of-18 (22.2 percent) from long distance this season. Powell is a career 39.6 percent three-point shooter and should have better shooting games in his future as he’s due for positive regression.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Ben Sheppard (knee) has been diagnosed with a torn left meniscus.
body: Sheppard was initially listed with a sore left knee, but the Pacers have since updated the injury report. With a torn meniscus, he’ll likely miss more time than the two weeks Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle initially said during his pregame media availability.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Sean Pedulla signed a two-way contract with the Sacramento Kings.
body: Sean Pedulla was waived by the Rockets on Monday and it didn’t take long for him to find another landing spot. The Ole Miss product has bounced was the G League Rookie of the Year last year averaging 23.6 points, 5.1 rebounds, 6.8 assists, 1.6 steals, shooting 44/37/85 shooting splits during the G League regular season. The Kings do not have a lot of point guard options outside of Darius Acuff and Malik Monk, who really isn’t a full time point guard. If there are injuries, Sean Pedulla might get some run and will be worth monitoring in deeper leagues.

headline: Mavericks head coach Dusty May said on Friday that Kyrie Irving’s minutes will be limited in Friday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Irving played 23 minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets, his first game since suffering a torn ACL on March 3, 2025. Given the time away from competitive basketball, Kyrie’s limited minutes are not a surprise. May did not disclose in his pregame availability whether Irving will be available for Saturday’s game against the Spurs.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jett Howard (calf) is out for Friday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Howard’s continued absence will not affect fantasy basketball, as he is not guaranteed to receive rotation minutes even if healthy.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: According to Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle, Ben Sheppard (knee) has no return timeline.
body: Despite the Pacers listing Sheppard as questionable for Friday’s game against the Mavericks, he’s expected to miss time with a left meniscus injury. Carlisle said on Friday that the reserve guard could miss two weeks or more. With Aaron Nesmith cleared to return from a strained hamstring, he’ll absorb most of the minutes that would have gone to Sheppard.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Pacers coach Rick Carlisle told reporters Aaron Nesmith (hamstring) will play in Friday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Nesmith will return after missing Wednesday’s win over the Pelicans, according to Pacers coach Rick Carlisle. With Nesmith back, Kelly Oubre Jr. will head to the bench for Friday’s game against the Mavericks.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports the Thunder have agreed on a two-way contract with Micah Peavy.
body: Peavy was waived by the Grizzlies earlier this week and went unclaimed. Now the former 18th overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft will try to carve out a role for himself on the Thunder. He reportedly picked Oklahoma City over Toronto as the Raptors had also offered him a two-way contract.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Felix Okpara (illness) is available for Friday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Okpara is available for Friday’s game, but that doesn’t guarantee he’ll see action. The rookie should only be rostered in dynasty leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Joel Embiid isn’t listed on the injury report for Saturday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Embiid told reporters after the win over the Cavaliers on Thursday that he will sit out one of the 76ers’ games this weekend. Given that he’s not listed on the injury report for Saturday’s game against the Bucks, it looks like he’ll play Saturday and sit out Sunday’s game against the Pistons. Adem Bona or Jabari Walker will likely start in Embiid’s absence.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Tyler Bilodeau (shoulder) is out for Saturday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Bilodeau’s continued absence will not affect fantasy basketball, as he is unlikely to receive consistent minutes in the rotation even when healthy.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jake LaRavia (ankle) is out for Friday’s game against the Clippers.
body: LaRavia was initially listed as questionable, but it should be no surprise that he’s been ruled out Friday after he sprained his right ankle in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors. The good news is that the injury isn’t considered serious and he should return to game action soon. Without LaRavia, Quentin Grimes could see enough minutes off the bench to be worth steaming consideration in category leagues.
author: Nick Shlain Quentin Grimes

headline: Brandin Podziemski (back) is probable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Podziemski is trending in the right direction after he was initially listed as questionable with a back ailment. He missed Wednesday’s loss against the Lakers with the same injury. Now that he’s been upgraded to probable, Podziemski, who appeared in all 82 games last season, should start alongside Stephen Curry against the Grizzlies Friday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Malik Monk (ankle) is available for Friday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Monk missed Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers, but was initially listed as probable for Friday’s tilt with the Trail Blazers. He’s since been upgraded to available and will play in tonight’s home opener. Monk should assume his typical role as a reserve guard for the Kings.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Charles Bassey (knee) is out for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Bassey will miss a second consecutive game as he continues to deal with patellar tendinitis in his right knee. Draymond Green started at center for Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, and he may be asked to do the same against Memphis.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trevon Brazile finished Thursday’s loss to the Thunder with four points (1-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs) and 12 rebounds.
body: In his official NBA debut, Brazile struggled from the field, missing all four of his three-point attempts. However, the second-round pick out of Arkansas was effective on the glass, leading the Nuggets with 12 rebounds. Brazile played 18 minutes, partly because Spencer Jones (hamstring) didn’t play. However, despite the perimeter shooting struggles, the rookie’s rebounding output was encouraging.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jordan Hawkins (illness) is available for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Hawkins is available to make his Bulls debut after sitting out Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors. However, as a two-way player, the former lottery pick isn’t guaranteed to see action against the Bucks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tobe Awaka (knee) is available for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Awaka was also on the injury report ahead of Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors, in which he played 14 minutes. Unless Friday’s game gets out of hand, the undrafted rookie out of Arizona will likely play fewer minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dailyn Swain (gastrointestinal illness) is available for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Swain is set to make his official Bulls debut after sitting out Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors. His availability may drop Jaylin Sellers out of the rotation entirely after the undrafted rookie played 14 minutes in the opener.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zach Collins (quad) is available for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Collins is available to play after being listed as probable on the initial injury report. Because of the time he missed during the preseason with the quad injury, he’ll likely be limited to 12-16 minutes. Collins played nine minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Josh Giddey (wrist) is available for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Giddey is good to go after being listed as probable on the Bulls’ initial injury report. He’ll take on his usual role as starting point guard, so managers rostering Giddey need to ensure he’s in their lineups before the 4 PM Eastern start time.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Taurean Prince (personal) is available for Friday’s game against the Heat.
body: Prince is available to make his Pistons’ debut after missing Tuesday’s win over the Celtics. While his status won’t significantly affect fantasy basketball, it could drop Ron Holland II out of the rotation entirely. Holland played three first-half minutes against the Celtics but saw no action after halftime, while Javonte Green played 18 second-half minutes and gave the Pistons a needed spark.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jock Landale (nose) is available for Friday’s game against the Hornets.
body: Landale, who played 19 minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s win over the Magic, is dealing with a broken nose. He’ll take on his usual responsibilities as Onyeka Okongwu’s backup, which limits the veteran center’s fantasy value.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Knicks and Dalton Knecht have agreed to a two-way contract.
body: The Lakers waived Knecht, the 17th overall pick in the 2024 draft, on Monday after two underwhelming seasons in Los Angeles. He certainly had his moments with the Lakers, but inconsistent offensive production and defensive struggles led to the 6-foot-6 wing ultimately falling out of the rotation. While Knecht may not get the minutes to impact fantasy basketball in New York, the two-way deal gives him a chance to work his way back into the NBA full-time.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dailyn Swain (gastrointestinal illness) and Jordan Hawkins (gastrointestinal illness) are probable for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Swain and Hawkins are on track to play Friday afternoon after sitting out Wednesday’s season-opening loss to the Raptors. Swain’s availability may push Jaylin Sellers out of the rotation after he logged 14 minutes off the bench in Toronto. Sellers and Hawkins are on two-way contracts, which limits how often the Bulls can activate them for games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nikola Jokić accounted for 13 points (5-of-19 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder.
body: Neither MVP winner in Thursday’s game played well in the first half. The difference was that while Oklahoma City’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander turned things around in the second half, Jokić could not. The Thunder big men deserve credit for their defense, but “The Joker” couldn’t find a rhythm. He and the Nuggets will look to bounce back when they host the Pelicans on Saturday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Joel Embiid said after Thursday’s win over the Cavaliers that he will miss one of the 76ers’ final two games of the week.
body: The 76ers were the only team with a four-game Week 1, which will conclude with a Saturday-Sunday back-to-back. Embiid sitting out one game of a back-to-back, especially this early in the season, is not a surprise. The only issue is that he didn’t reveal which game he’ll miss, with the 76ers hosting Milwaukee on Saturday and Detroit on Sunday. Given the strength of those teams, the Bucks may be the team that misses out on having to deal with “The Process.” Adem Bona or Jabari Walker could get a spot start, and LeBron James may spend a little more time at center as a small-ball alternative.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: DeMar DeRozan produced 13 points (5-of-9 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs) and two rebounds in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder.
body: DeRozan was used in a reserve role on Thursday, and that’s likely how he’ll be used on nights when the Nuggets are healthy. More importantly, he got 28 minutes in his Nuggets debut. DeRozan’s issues on Thursday: foul shooting and turnovers. In addition to missing three of six from the charity stripe, DeRozan recorded five turnovers. He’s averaged more than 2.5 turnovers per game once in his NBA career, so fantasy managers shouldn’t worry about Thursday’s number.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Aaron Gordon tallied 20 points (6-of-9 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder.
body: A notoriously poor perimeter shooter for most of his NBA career, Gordon has worked hard in recent years to change that. A 41 percent three-point shooter over his last two seasons, the Nuggets forward hit 3-of-4 from distance on Thursday. By comparison, the other starters shot a combined 3-of-15 from beyond the arc against the Thunder. No one should expect Gordon to challenge Stephen Curry, but his perimeter shot is no longer a liability.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Johnson (ankle) finished Thursday’s loss to the Thunder with five points (2-of-3 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer.
body: Johnson played 11 minutes in Thursday’s opener before a right ankle injury ended his night just before halftime. Officially, the veteran wing was questionable for the second half, but he never returned. Alpha Diallo (4/2/3/1) started the second half and played 22 minutes. If Nuggets head coach David Adelman prefers to keep DeMar DeRozan in the sixth man role, Diallo could start Saturday’s game against the Pelicans if Johnson can’t play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Christian Braun amassed seven points (3-of-10 FGs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder.
body: While injuries played a role last season, Braun’s scoring average dropped by more than three points compared to his 2024-25 output. Unfortunately, the Nuggets guard got off to a slow start on Thursday, shooting 3-of-10 from the field. Braun was active on the glass, but the overall production was disappointing.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jamal Murray recorded six points (2-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 Fts), 10 rebounds, three assists and one steal in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder.
body: Murray shot 2-of-9 from the field in the first half of Thursday’s season opener. Unfortunately for fantasy managers who likely believed that things couldn’t get worse in the second half, they did. Murray scored just one point after halftime and recorded more turnovers (four) than field-goal attempts (two). With the Nuggets playing just two games during Week 1, fantasy managers will hope to see Murray rebound on Saturday against the Pelicans.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nikola Jokić accounted for 13 points (5-of-19 FGs, 2-of-4 Fts), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Thursday’s loss ot the Thunder.
body: Neither MVP winner in Thursday’s game played well in the first half. The difference was that while Oklahoma City’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander turned things around in the second half, Jokić could not. The Thunder big men deserve credit for their defense, but “The Joker” couldn’t find a rhythm. He and the Nuggets will look to bounce back when they host the Pelicans on Saturday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ajay Mitchell amassed 12 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five steals and one blocked shot in Thursday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: While he may not be in the Thunder’s starting lineup, Mitchell can still provide solid fantasy value. He played 24 minutes against the Nuggets, doubling his point total from Tuesday’s win over the Spurs. More important for fantasy managers were the “stocks": Mitchell tallied six steals and blocks after recording none in San Antonio. Five-steal nights are unlikely to be the norm, but Mitchell can be close to a top-100 fantasy player for a second consecutive season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Chet Holmgren recorded 12 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 17 rebounds, two assists, one steal and four blocks in Thursday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: After blocking four shots in Tuesday’s season opener, Holmgren matched that mark on Thursday night. Add in the rebounds, and this was an excellent night for those rostering the slender 7-footer, especially in category leagues. The Western Conference Finals may have left a bad taste in Holmgren’s mouth, but he appears to have put that behind him. This could be a big season for Holmgren if he stays healthy.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Williams accounted for 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers in Thursday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: J-Dub was Oklahoma City’s top scorer in their home opener, leading the team with 21 points while shooting just under 50 percent from the field. Williams, who appeared in just 33 games last season, looked much sharper than he did in Tuesday’s season-opening win over the Spurs. If he stays healthy, J-Dub should deliver a top-50 season to fantasy managers at a minimum.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandin Podziemski (back) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Podziemski did not play in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, leading to De’Anthony Melton taking the starting spot. Melton played 21 minutes, while reserves Will Richard and Brandon Williams played 20 and 18 minutes, respectively. Expect a similar rotation if Podziemski can’t play on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Stewart, injured during the preseason, did not play in Wednesday’s win over the Jazz. Quinten Post logged 19 minutes off the bench as the backup center, and he’ll likely keep that role if Beef Stew can’t play on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cedric Coward (wrist) is doubtful for Friday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Coward, who played 28 minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Jazz, is dealing with a sprained left wrist. With the doubtful tag, he’s more likely to miss Friday. If Coward sits, reserves like Scotty Pippen Jr. and Jerami Grant would get more offensive opportunities.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bradley Beal (knee) is out for Friday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Beal will miss a second straight game due to right knee injury management. Kobe Sanders and Gradey Dick played rotation minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s win over the Kings, with the latter scoring 12 points in 19 minutes. Look for more of the same on Friday night.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Charles Bassey (knee) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Bassey did not play in Wednesday’s opener against the Lakers, leaving the Warriors light on options at center. With Kristaps Porziņģis (illness) out indefinitely, Draymond Green may spend more time at center than head coach Steve Kerr would prefer. Al Horford can provide depth off the bench, but he’s unlikely to exceed 20 minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Spencer Jones (hamstring) is out for Thursday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Jones, who strained his left hamstring early in training camp, is also navigating a right hamstring injury. His absence may give fellow reserve Trevon Brazile a few minutes, but it is unlikely to significantly affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Collin Sexton (leg) is not on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Sexton didn’t play in the preseason or the Lakers’ season-opening win over the Warriors, so the Lakers may monitor his minutes closely on Friday. Getting him back gives JJ Redick another option off the bench, which lacks on-ball playmakers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jake LaRavia (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Clippers.
body: LaRavia sprained his right ankle in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors, and team trainers helped him back to the locker room. With Cameron Carr (oblique) and Adou Thiero (knee) already out, LaRavia’s minutes will likely be split among Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams and Quentin Grimes if he can’t play on Friday. Despite coming off the bench, Grimes offers a higher category league ceiling than Thybulle or Williams.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Carr (oblique) and Adou Thiero (knee) are out for Friday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Neither Carr nor Thiero played in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors, and both are considered day-to-day moving forward. Their absences mean the Lakers will stick with a nine-man rotation, with backup center Kevon Looney as the ninth man.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Chris Youngblood (ankle) and Branden Carlson (concussion protocol) are out for Friday’s game against the Kings.
body: The continued absences of Youngblood and Carlson will not affect fantasy basketball, as neither is guaranteed rotation minutes when healthy.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dean Wade (ankle) is out for Thursday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Wade will miss a second consecutive game as he continues to recover from a sprained left ankle. As a result, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope may come close to the 26 minutes he played off the bench in Tuesday’s win over the Knicks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jarrett Allen (knee) is available for Thursday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Listed as questionable on the Cavaliers’ initial injury report for Thursday, Allen is good to go. He’ll start alongside James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson and Evan Mobley.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keldon Johnson (mouth) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Johnson suffered a laceration to his mouth during Tuesday’s loss to the Thunder, but he still played 20 minutes off the bench. He’ll likely carry a similar workload if he’s available on Friday. If Johnson can’t play, Harrison Barnes and Carter Bryant stand to gain the most in playing time.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tobias Harris (calf) is out for Friday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Harris, whose calf strain sidelined him for the entire preseason, will miss a second consecutive regular-season game. His absence means Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell will continue to start, and that may remain true even after Harris returns to action.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Aaron Fox (wrist) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Fox, who played 32 minutes in Tuesday’s season-opening loss to the Thunder, is dealing with a sprained right wrist. If there’s a silver lining to the injury, it’s that he shoots left-handed. If Fox can’t play on Friday, Julian Champagnie could move into the starting lineup after playing 30 minutes off the bench on Tuesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Reed Sheppard (knee) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Sheppard, who logged 16 minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks, is dealing with a bone bruise and contusion in his left knee. The third-year guard is effectively third in the Rockets’ point-guard pecking order behind Fred VanVleet and Marcus Smart, which hurts his fantasy value.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Steven Adams (calf) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Spurs.
body: A game-time call for Houston’s season opener, Adams did not play in Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks. Clint Capela effectively took over backup center duties, but he played just eight minutes. Rostering Capela would not be much of a gain for fantasy managers if Adams remains out on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Devin Carter (illness) is out for Friday’s game against the Knicks.
body: It was reported on Monday that Carter was dealing with mononucleosis, so he’s likely to be unavailable for a while. His continued absence does not affect fantasy basketball or the Celtics’ rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: T.J. McConnell (hamstring) is out Friday against the Mavericks.
body: McConnell will be out for a second straight game to open the 2026-27 campaign, which should lead to a bump in ball-handling responsibilities for Andrew Nembhard behind Tyrese Haliburton.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Felix Okpara (illness) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Okpara’s availability does not affect fantasy basketball or the Wizards’ rotation, as Anthony Davis, Alex Sarr and Deandre Ayton are all available to play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jonathan Isaac (knee) is out for Friday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Management of Isaac’s left knee injury will keep him out of a second consecutive game, but his continued absence won’t significantly impact the Magic rotation. Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain remain Orlando’s top two bench options at forward.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Black (ankle) is out for Friday’s matchup with the Timberwolves.
body: Black will miss a second straight game as he recovers from a right ankle sprain. In the season opener against the Hawks, Tristan da Silva had a productive showing off the bench across 28 minutes. He should be heavily involved in the rotation until Black returns.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Jett Howard (calf) is doubtful for Friday’s matchup with the Pacers.
body: Howard will miss a second consecutive game to open the 2026-27 campaign, and it’s unclear when he’ll be ready to return. His absence won’t impact fantasy basketball.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Dailyn Swain (gastrointestinal illness) and Jordan Hawkins (gastrointestinal illness) are questionable for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Due to the same ailment, Swain and Hawkins sat out Wednesday’s season-opening defeat in Toronto. As a result, undrafted rookie Jaylin Sellers played 14 minutes off the bench. With Sellers and Hawkins on two-way contracts, Swain may be the player with the best chance of logging rotation minutes if he’s available on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Josh Giddey (wrist) is probable for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Giddey, who struggled mightily in Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors, is dealing with a sprained left wrist. However, the probable tag suggests he’ll fill his usual starting point guard role. If Giddey can’t play, Tre Jones is the most likely replacement.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Caleb Martin (thumb) and Tarik Biberovic (heel) are out for Friday’s matchup with the Pacers.
body: Both players will miss a second straight game, though neither’s availability will make a difference in Dallas’ rotation. Fantasy managers can safely leave them on the waiver wire.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Zach Collins (quad) is probable for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Expected to be limited to 12-16 minutes in his first game back from a strained right quad, Collins played just nine minutes in Wednesday’s blowout loss to the Raptors. The probable tag suggests he’ll be available Friday to back up Jalen Smith. Until he can play without restrictions, Collins is unlikely to get the minutes needed to impact fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tobe Awaka (knee) is probable for Friday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Despite a sprained left MCL, Awaka played 14 minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors, grabbing 7 rebounds. The undrafted rookie may face a similar workload on Friday, especially with Zach Collins (quad) under a minutes limit.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Taurean Prince (personal) is probable for Friday’s matchup with the Heat.
body: Prince is poised to make his Pistons debut on Friday, but fantasy managers shouldn’t be tracking. His availability has little impact on Detroit’s rotation.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Cavs reporter Chris Fedor reports that Jarrett Allen says he will play against the 76ers on Thursday.
body: Allen has been dealing with right patellar tendinopathy, but he attended Thursday’s shootaround and said that he expects to play. In three matchups with the 76ers last season, Allen averaged 14.7 points, 7.3 rebounds and 2.3 “stocks.”
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: The Athletic’s Josh Robbins reports that AJ Dybantsa (ankle) is out for Friday’s home matchup with the Raptors.
body: Dybantsa will miss a second straight game due to a sprained left ankle, but the Wizards play the second leg of a back-to-back set on Saturday against the Bulls, which will give the rookie a quick turnaround to make his regular-season debut. Dybantsa could replace Bilal Coulibaly or Kyshawn George in the starting five when he finally gets back on the court.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Keegan Murray accounted for two points (1-of-8 FGs), four rebounds and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: Given Darius Acuff Jr.'s struggles on Wednesday, Murray’s night may avoid some scrutiny. However, he also struggled, missing his first seven attempts and not scoring until 9:08 remained in the fourth quarter. And Murray didn’t do much in the other categories either, which is a concern for fantasy managers. He’ll look to bounce back on Friday when the Kings host Portland.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Acuff Jr. amassed 12 points (5-of-24 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and three steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: Most fantasy managers and basketball fans expect rookie point guards to be inefficient. However, Acuff’s performance against the Clippers was rough. He missed all seven three-point attempts, shot 5-of-24 from the field, and finished with more turnovers (four) than assists (three). Acuff’s upside is undeniable, but he’ll have games like Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Domantas Sabonis finished Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers with 14 points (5-of-5 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 18 rebounds, eight assists and one steal.
body: Sabonis didn’t miss a shot on Wednesday and finished two assists shy of a triple-double. However, it’s fair to ask why he didn’t get more shots, especially when Darius Acuff Jr. and Keegan Murray combined to shoot 6-of-32 from the field. Playing alongside a rookie point guard can be challenging for a veteran post player like Sabonis, who can also facilitate offense. However, Wednesday’s outing showed he can offer excellent fantasy value on nights with low shot attempts.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zach LaVine recorded 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: After injuries limited him to 39 games in his first full season with the Kings, LaVine looked completely healthy on Wednesday. Without him and fellow veteran Domantas Sabonis, the Kings would have fared worse, but they still lost the opener 121-96. As long as he stays healthy, LaVine should return to being a reliable fantasy asset. The question is whether a good first half of the season would convince a contending team to acquire him before the February trade deadline.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keaton Wagler notched 15 points (4-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
body: In a matchup of lottery picks, Wagler had a much better night than Sacramento’s Darius Acuff Jr. The former Illinois standout played 29 minutes off the bench, sharing the court with Darius Garland and taking a few short stints as the lone playmaker. Wagler was efficient, and while you shouldn’t overreact to one game, it wouldn’t hurt to add him now if he’s on the waiver wire in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brook Lopez accumulated 17 points (7-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 11 rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
body: Despite coming off the bench, Lopez played 27 minutes on Wednesday due to starting center Isaiah Jackson getting into foul trouble. The veteran 7-footer clearly still has something left in the tank, as he recorded a complete stat line that included a double-double. Jackson still hasn’t established himself as a center you can fully trust in fantasy basketball, which is a good reason to roster Lopez in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Rui Hachimura tallied 10 points (3-of-13 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
body: Given the Clippers’ lack of proven scorers, Hachimura is in a position to offer more value than he did as a Laker. However, you have to make shots, and he didn’t do that consistently enough on Wednesday. Hachimura shot 1-of-6 from inside the arc, which hurt his field-goal percentage. He did put up decent numbers in rebounds, steals and blocked shots, so Wednesday wasn’t a total loss for those rostering Hachimura.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Jackson accounted for 13 points (6-of-8 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds and one steal in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
body: Jackson’s starting nod was expected to raise his fantasy ceiling, and he was productive Wednesday night. However, the Clippers’ center played just 15 minutes because of foul trouble. Backup Brook Lopez played 27 minutes, and that may not have happened if Jackson were able to stay on the court. Jackson is worth a look in 12-team leagues if he’s on the waiver wire, even with the foul trouble against Sacramento.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Garland finished Wednesday’s win over the Kings with 30 points (11-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and three three-pointers.
body: After a tumultuous offseason for the franchise, the Clippers got their 2026-27 off to a good start on Wednesday. Garland dominated his individual matchup against Kings rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr., scoring an efficient 30 points. Matchups will get tougher as the season progresses, but fantasy managers hope Garland delivers performances of this caliber more often.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scoot Henderson accounted for 15 points (7-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Suns.
body: Among the four guards in Portland’s rotation, Henderson (19 minutes) played the least on Wednesday. He played nine of those minutes after halftime, while starters Ja Morant and Damian Lillard and reserve Jrue Holiday (8/4/1/2) logged between seven and nine minutes each. While Henderson having a role won’t be an issue for him, his playing time might be, especially against tougher opponents.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Micah Potter (illness) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Suns.
body: Potter has been dealing with an illness, but was trending in the right direction today and has been ruled in for matchup with the Suns. As merely a depth option for the Trail Blazers, Potter is unlikely to play significant minutes Wednesday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Deni Avdija (ankle) will start against Suns.
body: Deni will give it a go and start in the Blazers first game of the season. He’s looking to build upon his All-Star season last year and lead the Blazers back to the playoffs.

headline: Tari Eason was ejected from Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks after being assessed a Flagrant 2 foul.
body: Due to his decision to push Mavericks forward P.J. Washington, Eason played just three minutes in Wednesday’s opener before receiving his marching orders. The Rockets forward finished with two points (1-of-2 FGs), one rebound and one steal.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephen Curry (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers.
body: No surprise here as Curry was listed as probable with an ankle injury. The 38-year-old point guard appeared to suffer the injury during Sunday’s open practice. Curry’s now officially good to go for the season opener against the Lakers.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson will start Wednesday’s game against the Kings.
body: Dunn is good to go after missing most of the preseason with a minor injury, and he’ll start alongside Garland in the backcourt. Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue said on Saturday that Jackson would start at center, so his inclusion is unsurprising. Garland and Hachimura should lead the starters offensively.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Malik Monk (ankle) is doubtful for Wednesday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Initially questionable for Wednesday’s season opener, Monk’s status is trending in the wrong direction. If he can’t play, rookie Emanuel Sharp’s role could expand, but he won’t be worth the streaming risk in most leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said on Wednesday that he’s hopeful Brandin Podziemski (back) will return for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: After missing practice on Monday, Podziemski will miss Wednesday’s opener against the Lakers due to lower back soreness. However, he may not be out long, with Kerr hoping Podz can play on Friday. De’Anthony Melton is the player whose role may expand the most while Podziemski sits.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luke Kennard (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Kennard will miss the Suns’ season opener after initially being listed as questionable. His absence likely means fellow reserve Jordan Goodwin will get more minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Adou Thiero (knee) has been shut down for a few days after experiencing swelling.
body: Thiero will not play in Wednesday’s opener against the Warriors due to a right knee effusion. There has also been some swelling in the knee, so the Lakers are shutting the second-year wing down for a few days. Upon his clearance to resume working out, Thiero will be considered day-to-day.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Deni Avdija (ankle) is a game time decision against the Suns in Wednesday’s season opener.
body: The Blazers already have Shaedon Sharpe out for an extended of of time. If Deni were to miss time, there would be more minutes for Sidy Cissoko and Vit Krecji, but neither would be that impactful in most fantasy leagues.

headline: According to Lakers head coach JJ Redick, Cameron Carr (oblique) is “ramping up” and is day-to-day moving forward.
body: Carr, who played well during Summer League, was ruled out for Wednesday’s opener with a strained oblique. The good news is that a return to action may not be far away, with the rookie now considered day-to-day, according to Redick. Carr should slide into the back end of the Lakers’ perimeter rotation once cleared to play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyrie Irving, Max Christie, Cooper Flagg, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Wednesday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Christie and Flagg were the only starters to take on that role in the Mavericks’ final game of the 2025-26 season. Irving, Washington, and Gafford are back from injury and will round out the starting five on Opening Night. It’s unclear whether Irving’s minutes will be limited, but don’t be surprised if the Mavericks don’t ask him to take on a full workload immediately.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Rockets start Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun against the Mavericks on Wednesday.
body: Durant is 38 and entering his 19th season in the NBA, but he showed few signs of slowing down last season as he was named to the league’s All-NBA second-team. He’ll start alongside VanVleet, Thompson, Smith and Sengun against the Mavericks on Wednesday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Julian Phillips (illness) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Phillips is good to go after initially being questionable for Wednesday’s season opener. However, with the Rockets largely healthy on the perimeter, the two-way contract wing is unlikely to get the minutes needed to affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Steven Adams (calf) is a game time decision against the Mavs
body: If Adams were to miss time, Clint Capela will likely end up taking the backup center minutes for the Rockets. Adams isn’t likely to impact most fantasy leagues anyway.

headline: Dru Smith (calf) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves.
Myron Gardner (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves.
The Wizards will start Trae Young, Kyshawn George, Bilal Coulibaly, Anthony Davis, and Alex Sarr against Bucks on Wednesday
body: Bilal Coulibaly will take the starting spot of AJ Dybantsa who rolled his ankle in the final pre-season game against the Pelicans. Bilal is worth a stream spot in redraft leagues if he’s available.
